question: What is the primary purpose of patient assessment documentation?

options.A: To replace verbal handovers entirely in the ward
options.B: To determine the financial salary of hospital staff
options.C: To provide research data for pharmaceutical companies
options.D: To ensure continuity of care among healthcare providers

explanation: Documentation acts as the central communication link for all team members caring for the patient over time. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is establishing a baseline of health status through documentation important?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any future physical examinations
options.B: It helps track patient responses to clinical interventions
options.C: It guarantees complete recovery within forty-eight hours
options.D: It proves the patient has no underlying chronic illnesses

explanation: Initial baseline data allows nurses to measure whether a patient is improving or deteriorating after treatment begins. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h1)

question: The legal phrase associated with poor or absent nursing records is care not documented is...
explanation: Legally, if an action is missing from the patient record, courts assume the action never took place. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h2)

question: A nurse realizes an assessment was missed during the morning shift and wants to record it hours later. What is the correct action?

options.A: Write a late entry indicating the exact current time and the time of the missed assessment
options.B: Insert the missed notes between previous lines to keep the page tidy
options.C: Skip documenting the assessment since too much time has already passed
options.D: Backdate the entry to match the exact time the assessment should have occurred

explanation: Late entries must clearly state when they are being written and what time period they cover to maintain transparency. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which documentation format organizes notes using Subjective, Objective, Assessment, and Plan?
explanation: SOAP is an acronym representing subjective findings, objective findings, clinical assessment, and the proposed care plan. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the main characteristic of Charting by Exception?

options.A: Only doctors are allowed to write progress notes in the file
options.B: Only abnormal findings or deviations from norms are written down
options.C: Every single routine vital sign must be written in a long story
options.D: Patient assessments are performed only once a week

explanation: Charting by exception saves time by assuming normal parameters unless a specific exception is explicitly recorded. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which item belongs to the objective component of a comprehensive assessment record?

options.A: The patient's personal history of past anxiety
options.B: The patient's description of severe chest pain
options.C: Measured blood pressure and temperature readings
options.D: A family member's complaint about hospital food

explanation: Objective data consists of measurable and observable facts gathered through physical examination and diagnostic tools. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why must risk assessment tools for falls and pressure ulcers be included in documentation?

options.A: To fulfill insurance billing requirements without affecting care
options.B: To guide preventive nursing interventions and protect patient safety
options.C: To prove that the hospital has adequate furniture and beds
options.D: To replace the need for physical assessments by physicians

explanation: Documenting risk scores helps nurses initiate specific protective measures before complications like falls or bedsores occur. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which entry demonstrates the best example of objective nursing documentation?

options.A: Patient is uncooperative and lazy about taking morning medications
options.B: Patient had a terrible night and complained constantly
options.C: Patient looks very anxious and is crying loudly for no reason
options.D: Patient vomited 200 mL of green-tinged fluid at 0800 hours

explanation: This statement records measurable quantities and specific observable events without subjective judgment or emotional labeling. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h5)

question: When should nursing assessments and interventions ideally be documented?

options.A: As close to the time of occurrence as possible
options.B: Only after the patient has been discharged home
options.C: Whenever the head nurse demands chart audits
options.D: At the very end of the working week

explanation: Timely documentation prevents reliance on faulty memory and ensures real-time communication for patient safety. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h5)

question: What does charting ahead involve, which makes it a serious documentation error?

options.A: Recording nursing actions before they are actually performed
options.B: Documenting vital signs immediately after taking them
options.C: Writing notes for the next shift before handing over
options.D: Submitting assessment reports prior to doctor'valuation

explanation: Charting ahead is fraudulent and dangerous because planned interventions can be cancelled or altered unexpectedly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which recorded phrase should a nurse avoid because it represents a subjective judgment?

options.A: Patient is uncooperative and difficult to manage
options.B: Patient refused the prescribed 10 PM oral analgesic
options.C: Patient's urine output measured 150 mL in six hours
options.D: Patient smelled strongly of alcohol upon admission

explanation: Labeling a patient as uncooperative is subjective and vague; nurses should instead describe the specific behaviors observed. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h6)

question: What regulation in Nigeria sets standards for processing and protecting personal health data?
explanation: The NDPR provides the legal framework for safeguarding personal data privacy, including electronic health records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which action represents a direct breach of patient confidentiality by a nurse?

options.A: Storing physical folders inside a locked nurses' station cabinet
options.B: Discussing a patient's diagnosis in the public hospital cafeteria
options.C: Sharing clinical notes with the primary attending physician
options.D: Logging out of the electronic health record terminal before leaving

explanation: Discussing patient details in public spaces exposes confidential information to unauthorized persons, violating privacy ethics. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h7)
